_: Region sheet for dunmer-north (2.5a1b). Talk is seeded from the region's published place records; every trait cites a lore dossier or says inferred.

norms.text: Two peoples share the towns: Argonian quarters on the marsh side, Dunmer compounds on the dry ground above them.
Saltrice is grown in fields, the nearest thing the province has to farming as outsiders know it.
Money moves at the border; a guard who looks away expects payment.
Hatchlings of the old families were born at the Hatching Pools and their egg records are kept there.
Argonians here speak as Argonians do elsewhere and rarely contract; the Dunmer and Imperial habits of the towns do not set their speech.

taboos.text: Asking a mixed family on which side of the coffles its grandparents stood.
Lighting a fire on peat ground; the Great Burn started outside Stormhold.

values.text: Title to land, argued field by field since the Dres left.
Living alongside outsiders without liking them, as Stormhold always has.
Magic as a survival skill learned at home, not in a hall.

contempts.text: Slavers; the Telvanni who kept taking Argonians after the Pact forbade it.
Archein families who managed the raids and now manage the fields.

place.text: The north is dry enough to farm and old enough to have ruins stacked three deep.

work.text: Field work pays here, which it does nowhere else in the marsh.

people.text: A neighbour may be Dunmer; that says little about whose side his family took.

faction.text: The Ash-Reed Accord argues saltrice title; the Dres heirs still have papers.

hist.text: The Hist at the Pools is the region's; outsiders go to Hissmir to touch a tree.

empire.text: The Empire fought the Dres here and left both sides worse off.

trade.text: The Tear road and the border river carry saltrice north and goods south.

danger.text: Crocodiles come inside town limits; the fens south of Stormhold are worse.

rumour.text: Crystals still come out of the tunnels under Stormhold.

directions.text: Ways are given by the trunk road: Stormhold, Tenmar Wall, Alten Corimont, Riverwalk, Thorn.

addressTerms.text: Dunmer residents use sera among themselves and for the polite stranger.
Argonians call outsiders ojel. Morrowind visitors are named by their House.

neverSaid.text: That the Accession War is over; everyone says it, few believe it.

grievances.text: Thorn's field-owners and the stewards of Hissmir both claim the toll on the pilgrim water.
No court has settled who owns the saltrice fields that the Dres left.

rumours.text: The Telvanni still buy across the river, through Archein middlemen.
The flooding round the wamasu pond is worse this year than in any year people remember.

views.text: The interior is where the trees are; northerners go there to pray, not to trade.
The upriver camps sell labour by the roll; the north sold people once and knows the shape.
Archon is a short sail and a fair harbour; coast folk keep their word on a cargo.
Gideon's people talk like Cyrodiil and trade with Leyawiin; they are far off.
